operons-lac-trp.alt: Four panels, each showing a promoter P, an operator O and structural genes. Lac operon with no lactose: the repressor made by the separate lacI gene sits on the operator and RNA polymerase is blocked, so the genes lacZ, lacY and lacA are off. Lac operon with lactose: allolactose binds the repressor, which changes shape and leaves the operator; RNA polymerase, helped by cAMP-CAP bound beside the promoter, makes one mRNA for all three genes. Trp operon with little tryptophan: the repressor is inactive and RNA polymerase copies the five genes for making tryptophan. Trp operon with plenty of tryptophan: tryptophan binds and activates the repressor, which binds the operator and blocks transcription.
